question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Locations and Clive's early actions in the Second Carnatic War]
options: Madras (Fort St. George) — Where Clive served as a writer before joining the military company
Arcot — Capital of the Carnatic which Clive captured with just 210 men in September 1751
Trichinopoly — Fort where Clive was besieged and held captive by Dupleix until the end of the war
Arni — Site of a victory where Clive defeated a superior force under Raju Sahib (Chanda Sahib's son) and French troops
wrong_fact: Clive was never besieged or held captive at Trichinopoly during the Second Carnatic War; he was the British officer who launched the diversion at Arcot and later helped relieve the siege of Trichinopoly from the outside.
explanation: In 1751, the French-backed Chanda Sahib besieged the British ally Muhammad Ali at Trichinopoly. Robert Clive proposed a bold diversionary attack on Arcot, Chanda Sahib's capital. With a tiny force of 200 Europeans and 300 sepoys (reduced by casualties to 210 men total during operations), Clive captured Arcot, withstood a 53-day siege, and then defeated Raju Sahib's forces at Arni and Kaveripakkam.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Battles and strategic geography of Clive's campaigns in 1751–1752]
options: Kaveripakkam (Covrepauk) — Battle where Clive defeated Raju Sahib's forces in a night action, destroying the French artillery
Conjeveram (Kanchipuram) — Temple town occupied by Clive to secure his communications between Arcot and Madras
Samiaveram — North of the Coleroon River, where Clive established a camp and survived a surprise attack by French-backed forces
Pondicherry — Fortified city captured by Robert Clive in 1752, resulting in the surrender of Dupleix
wrong_fact: Pondicherry was not captured by Robert Clive in 1752; it remained the French stronghold and capital until the Third Carnatic War, when it was captured by Eyre Coote in 1761. Dupleix was recalled by the French government in 1754, not forced to surrender Pondicherry to Clive.
explanation: Clive's campaign of 1751-1752 was localized around Madras, Arcot, and the Trichinopoly region. He occupied Kanchipuram (Conjeveram) to protect supply lines. He defeated Chanda Sahib's son at Kaveripakkam. At Samiaveram, near Trichinopoly, Clive established a blocking position to cut off French forces on Srirangam Island. Pondicherry itself was never captured or besieged by Clive during this war.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Specific geographic maneuvers and tactical decisions by Robert Clive during the Second Carnatic War]
options: Volkondah (Valikondapuram) — Clive's first independent command where he successfully stormed the hilltop fort against French commander d'Auteuil
Pichanda (Pitchandah) — Fortified temple north of the Seringham island captured by Clive to cut off French supply lines
Seringham (Srirangam Island) — Island between the Cauvery and Coleroon rivers where Clive and Lawrence trapped the French army under Law
Fort St. David (Cuddalore) — British base from which Clive's expedition to Arcot was authorized and supplied
wrong_fact: Volkondah was not Clive's first independent command, nor did he successfully storm it. It was the site of a humiliating British retreat under Captain Gingen earlier in 1751. Clive's first independent command was the expedition to Arcot.
explanation: In early 1751, British forces under Captain Gingen suffered a severe defeat and retreated at Volkondah. Clive, who was present as a civilian commissioner, witnessed the incompetence and resolved to take a military commission. His first independent command was the capture of Arcot. Later in 1752, Clive and Lawrence successfully trapped the French under Jacques Law at Seringham Island and captured Pichanda to isolate them, leading to a major French surrender.
